name: Alabama
description: Alabama requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has a lemon law that covers new vehicles purchased or leased in Alabama, and does not require emissions testing statewide.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
lemonLawSummary: Alabama gives a new-car buyer a lemon-law rights period of one year or 12,000 miles, whichever comes first, under Ala. Code §§ 8-20A-1(8) and 8-20A-2. The repair presumption is measured over 24 months or 24,000 miles, and at least one repair attempt has to fall inside that first year or 12,000 miles. The law treats the car as having had a reasonable number of attempts after three repairs of the same problem plus a final try by the manufacturer, or after 30 calendar days out of service, counting that final try. Before a lawsuit, send the manufacturer certified mail; once the presumption is already in place, the manufacturer gets seven calendar days to name a shop and 14 calendar days after you drop the car off to fix it.
registrationFeeRange: $23 for an automobile
registrationNotes: A designated agent and a licensing official may each add a $1.50 commission. Some counties add a local fee. Ala. Code § 40-12-242 sets the automobile fee.
lemonArbitration: Alabama has no lemon-law hearing board. A refund or replacement demand under Ala. Code § 8-20A-2 is a civil action that follows the certified-mail notice to the manufacturer.

name: Alaska
description: Alaska has some of the most unique vehicle ownership requirements in the nation. While liability insurance is mandatory, the state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections for most vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Under AS 45.45.320, Alaska measures the presumption during the express warranty or the year after delivery to the original owner, whichever ends first, and the statute sets no mileage cap. Three repairs of the same problem, if it is still there, or 30 business days in the shop, is enough attempts. Days when the shop cannot work for reasons outside its control do not count. To demand a refund or replacement, mail written notice before 60 days have passed after the warranty or that one-year period ends; the manufacturer then has 30 days to try one last repair.
registrationFeeRange: $100 for most vehicles
registrationNotes: Registration is biennial. There is no state sales tax. Some municipalities charge a local tax on a vehicle purchase.
lemonArbitration: No Alaska office arbitrates these warranty disputes. After the written demand in AS 45.45.320, the owner enforces a refund or replacement by filing suit.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Arizona
description: Arizona vehicle owners benefit from relatively low insurance minimums but must comply with emissions testing in the Phoenix and Tucson metro areas. The state offers incentives for electric and alternative fuel vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Arizona measures lemon-law repairs under Ariz. Rev. Stat. §§ 44-1262 and 44-1264 during the shorter of the express warranty or two years and 24,000 miles after the car was delivered. The presumption is four repairs of the same defect that still exists, or 30 calendar days the car spends out of service. Before that presumption can be used, the manufacturer has to have received direct written notice of the defect. It also has to have had a chance to repair the car.
emissionsDetails: The Phoenix area tests every two years. The Tucson area tests annually. The OBD test fee is $16.15 in both areas. The older tailpipe test is $15.20 in Phoenix and $12.25 in Tucson. The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality publishes these fees. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationFeeRange: $8 base fee plus vehicle license tax
registrationNotes: The vehicle license tax starts at 60 percent of the manufacturer base retail price. The value then drops 16.25 percent each year. The minimum tax is $10.
lemonArbitration: Arizona leaves the lemon-law remedy in court. The manufacturer must already have received the direct written notice required by Ariz. Rev. Stat. §§ 44-1262 and 44-1264.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Arkansas
description: Arkansas requires liability insurance and has a lemon law protecting new vehicle buyers. The state does not mandate emissions testing or a periodic safety inspection.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Arkansas runs its quality period to 24 months or 24,000 miles, whichever is later, in Ark. Code §§ 4-90-403(12), 4-90-406, and 4-90-410. After three tries at the same problem that substantially impairs the car, or one try at a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, send certified or registered mail so the manufacturer can make a final repair. A presumption also arises if that path was followed and the problem remains, if the car spent 30 calendar days in the shop, or if there were five or more attempts on separate occasions at problems that together substantially impair use and value. The manufacturer has ten days after the letter to offer a shop and ten days after you deliver the car to fix it; if it misses those deadlines, the final-attempt requirement drops and the presumption can no longer be rebutted.
registrationFeeRange: $17 up to 3,000 lb, $25 from 3,001 to 4,500 lb, or $30 above 4,500 lb
registrationNotes: That plate amount is the validation decal. A tag transfer is $1. An annual personal property assessment applies.
lemonArbitration: Arkansas does not substitute a state panel for the courts. The certified or registered letter in Ark. Code §§ 4-90-406 and 4-90-410 is the manufacturer's last repair chance before that case.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: California
description: California has the most comprehensive vehicle regulations in the country, including strict emissions standards, generous EV incentives, and strong consumer protection laws including a robust lemon law.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: California's Tanner presumption is Cal. Civ. Code § 1793.22. It applies during the first 18 months after delivery or the first 18,000 miles, whichever comes first. Within that time, two repairs of a defect likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, four repairs of the same defect, or more than 30 calendar days in the shop is a reasonable number of attempts. Direct notice to the manufacturer is required for the two-repair and four-repair counts only when the warranty or owner's manual clearly told the buyer to send it.
emissionsDetails: California requires biennial smog checks for vehicles older than eight model years in most areas. The state sets its own emissions standards through CARB, which are stricter than federal standards. Testing typically costs $30-$70. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: California's statewide CVRP rebate closed November 8, 2023. Income-qualified residents who scrap an older vehicle can apply for Clean Cars 4 All (cleancars4all.arb.ca.gov) before buying, and many California utilities offer EV charger rebates and EV rates.
registrationNotes: The registration fee includes a $3 alternative fuel and technology fee. That title amount is the transfer fee. A title-only application is $28. Replacement plates are $28. A separate CHP fee is $34. The vehicle license fee is 0.65 percent of value.
lemonArbitration: The Department of Consumer Affairs Arbitration Certification Program certifies manufacturer dispute programs under Cal. Civ. Code § 1793.22. A buyer may use a certified program and may still sue, including in small claims court.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A model year 2020 or later zero-emission vehicle pays a $121 road improvement fee at renewal. That fee is not charged on the first registration of a new zero-emission vehicle bought from a licensed dealer.

name: Colorado
description: Colorado combines mandatory liability insurance with emissions testing in the Denver metro area. The state is a leader in EV incentives, offering substantial tax credits for electric vehicle purchases.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: For vehicles sold or leased on or after August 7, 2024, Colo. Rev. Stat. § 42-10-103, as amended by SB 24-192, uses the first two years or 24,000 miles. Three repairs of the same problem, two repairs of a safety-based problem, or 24 business days out of service is the presumption, and the problem has to still be there. The manufacturer needs prior written notice by certified mail and then has ten business days after receiving it to try a cure. That cure counts as one repair.
emissionsDetails: Gasoline vehicles in all or parts of Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas, Jefferson, Larimer, and Weld counties are tested every two years. The newest vehicles are exempt for seven model years. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Colorado offers a state EV tax credit of $750 in 2026 for new EVs with an MSRP up to $80,000, plus an additional $2,500 for EVs with an MSRP under $35,000 (Colorado Energy Office). Dealers can apply the credit at purchase. Leases must be at least two years.
registrationFeeRange: Based on weight and specific ownership tax
registrationNotes: Specific ownership tax declines as the vehicle ages. Registration is annual.
lemonArbitration: Colorado certifies no state board to hear Colo. Rev. Stat. § 42-10-103 claims. Once the certified-mail cure period ends, the buyer files a civil action.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: The Colorado DMV lists a plug-in electric vehicle fee of $63.05. It also lists a road-usage charge of $26 for a battery-electric vehicle from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

name: Connecticut
description: Connecticut requires emissions testing for most vehicles and has strong consumer protection laws. The state mandates relatively high insurance minimums compared to the national average.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Connecticut's lemon law is Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42-179. The ordinary presumption runs during the first two years or 24,000 miles: four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, if the problem continues. A defect likely to cause death or serious injury uses a shorter window, the express warranty or one year after delivery, and it takes two repairs. You do not have to notify the manufacturer unless the warranty or the owner's manual clearly says written notice is required.
emissionsDetails: Connecticut tests registered vehicles every two years. The emissions test fee is $20. Vehicles younger than four model years are exempt. Model year 2001 and older vehicles are exempt. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Connecticut's CHEAPR program offers $1,500 for new battery EVs (from October 15, 2026) and $500 for plug-in hybrids at participating dealers. Income-qualified Rebate+ buyers can receive up to $4,500 on a new battery EV.
registrationNotes: The same passenger row lists a $10 administrative fee and a $15 Clean Air Act fee. The Passport to the Parks fee on that row is $24. A vehicle four years old or newer pays a $40 emissions exemption fee. A vehicle with a certificate of origin pays a $15 greenhouse gas fee.
usedCarLemonLaw: Connecticut's used-car dealer warranty is Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42-221. A dealer selling a used car for $3,000 to under $5,000, less than seven model years old, must warrant that it stays mechanically operational for 30 days or 1,500 miles, and a car sold for $5,000 or more gets 60 days or 3,000 miles. Department of Consumer Protection arbitration under § 42-181 covers new-car manufacturer disputes under § 42-179, not this used-car dealer warranty.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Delaware
description: Delaware requires liability insurance and biennial vehicle inspections. The state has no sales tax on vehicle purchases, which can represent significant savings for car buyers.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Del. Code tit. 6, § 5004 covers a new car for the warranty term or the first year after delivery, whichever ends first. Mileage does not cut that period short. The presumption is in place when substantially the same problem has been repaired four times and is still there, or when the car has been out of service for more than 30 calendar days. Use it against the manufacturer only after the manufacturer got a direct written notice and a chance to fix the car.
emissionsDetails: The emissions test covers New Castle, Kent, and Sussex counties. Vehicles in the first seven model years are excluded. Model year 1996 and newer gasoline vehicles use an OBD-II test. The inspection is free for Delaware residents. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Delaware inspects vehicles every two years before renewal. Vehicles in the first seven model years are excluded. The DMV conducts the inspection. Required inspections are free for Delaware residents.
registrationNotes: The document fee is 5.25 percent of the purchase price or NADA value. A duplicate plate with a sticker is $10. A plug-in hybrid under 6,000 pounds pays an additional $85 a year. A non-plug-in hybrid under 6,000 pounds pays an additional $60 a year.
lemonArbitration: Delaware has no lemon-law arbitrator on the state payroll. The direct written notice in Del. Code tit. 6, § 5004 is required before a court claim against the manufacturer.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric or fuel-cell vehicle under 6,000 pounds pays an additional $110 a year.

name: Florida
description: Florida is a no-fault insurance state, meaning your own insurance covers your injuries regardless of who caused the accident. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $10,000 personal injury protection (PIP) / $10,000 property damage liability. Bodily injury liability is not required to register a private car. It is required for taxis, to reinstate under the Financial Responsibility Law (10/20/10), and after a DUI conviction (100/300/50).
lemonLawSummary: Fla. Stat. §§ 681.102(9) and 681.104 give a rights period of 24 months after delivery, and the statute does not use a mileage cap. The presumption is three repairs of the same problem plus a final attempt by the manufacturer, if that attempt is undertaken, or 30 cumulative days out of service, 60 for a recreational vehicle. When the car has been out of service for 15 days, send written notice by registered or express mail so the manufacturer can inspect or repair. After three attempts on the same problem, a separate written notice gives the manufacturer one last repair.
registrationFeeRange: $14.50 - $32.50 based on weight
registrationNotes: The initial registration fee is $225. Florida calls that charge the new wheels on the road fee. An original used electronic title is $85.25. A lien fee of $2 may be added.
lemonArbitration: The Attorney General's Lemon Law Arbitration Division forwards eligible cases to the Florida New Motor Vehicle Arbitration Board under Fla. Stat. § 681.109. The request must arrive within 60 days after the rights period ends, or within 30 days after a certified manufacturer program finishes, whichever date is later, and a three-member panel hears it.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Georgia
description: Georgia requires liability insurance and annual emissions testing for gasoline cars and light trucks in 13 metro Atlanta counties. The state replaced its traditional sales tax on vehicles with a one-time title ad valorem tax (TAVT).
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Georgia's lemon law, O.C.G.A. §§ 10-1-782 and 10-1-784, ends the rights period at two years or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. One unsuccessful repair of a serious safety defect, three unsuccessful repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service counts as a reasonable number of attempts. After that, notify the manufacturer. It then has 28 days from receiving the notice to try one last repair.
emissionsDetails: Gasoline cars and light trucks in Cherokee, Clayton, Cobb, Coweta, DeKalb, Douglas, Fayette, Forsyth, Fulton, Gwinnett, Henry, Paulding, and Rockdale counties are tested every year. For 2026 registration, that covers model years 2002 through 2023. The three newest model years and vehicles 25 model years or older are exempt. A test costs up to $25. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationFeeRange: $20 for most vehicles
registrationNotes: The title ad valorem tax is 7 percent of fair market value on a standard purchase. A new resident pays 3 percent. A replacement plate or decal is $8.
lemonArbitration: Georgia's Attorney General Consumer Protection Division runs state-operated arbitration and does not represent either party. The application is due within 12 months after the lemon-law rights period ends.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Georgia DOR lists an annual alternative fuel vehicle fee of $238.59 for a non-commercial vehicle from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. It applies to every vehicle that runs only on electricity, and to a plug-in hybrid only if it carries an alternative fuel vehicle plate. It is in addition to the $20 registration fee.

name: Hawaii
description: Hawaii requires all registered vehicles to pass a periodic safety inspection. The state has mandatory no-fault insurance and offers growing incentives for electric vehicles as part of its clean energy goals.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $10,000 PIP
lemonLawSummary: Hawaii's lemon law, Haw. Rev. Stat. §§ 481I-2 and 481I-3, sets the rights period as the express warranty, two years, or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. Three exams or repairs of the same problem, one exam or repair of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption. The manufacturer has to have received a written report and a reasonable chance to repair. A dealer also notifies the manufacturer after a second report or after the car has been out more than 20 business days.
emissionsDetails: Hawaii's periodic inspection is a safety check under HRS § 286-26. It is not an emissions test. The inspection looks at the exhaust system because a noncompliant muffler fails the safety check.
safetyInspectionDetails: Hawaii requires a periodic safety inspection under HRS § 286-26. Most passenger vehicles are inspected every 12 months. A new vehicle does not need that annual inspection until two years after its first inspection. Since July 1, 2025, the fee is $25.75 for automobiles and trucks.
registrationFeeRange: $46 a year plus county weight tax
registrationNotes: Honolulu charges $10 to transfer a title within 30 days. Hawaii County charges $5. Alternative-fuel vehicles pay an extra $50. An electric vehicle is excluded from that alternative-fuel surcharge. HRS § 249-31 sets the state registration fee.
lemonArbitration: Hawaii's Regulated Industries Complaints Office at the Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs administers the State Certified Arbitration Program. A consumer applies there for a refund or replacement decision on a new-car warranty dispute.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Since July 1, 2025, Hawaii electric vehicles pay a state road usage charge at registration renewal instead of the alternative-fuel surcharge. Owners can choose 0.8 cents a mile, capped at $50 a year, or a flat $50 through June 30, 2028. After that, the per-mile charge is required.

name: Idaho
description: Idaho requires 25/50/15 liability coverage and verifies insurance electronically. The state repealed its Treasure Valley emissions testing requirement effective July 1, 2023. Vehicles are titled and registered through county DMV offices, with state registration fees based on vehicle age.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Idaho Code § 48-903 looks at the express warranty, two years, or 24,000 miles, whichever date comes first. If the problem was first reported during the warranty, repair attempts within three years of delivery can still support a refund or replacement. Four repairs of the same problem, 30 business days out of service, or one repair of a complete brake or steering failure likely to cause death or serious injury, is the presumption, and the manufacturer still gets one chance to repair that brake or steering failure. The four-repair and 30-day paths apply against the manufacturer only after written notice and a chance to cure.
emissionsDetails: Idaho repealed its vehicle inspection and maintenance (emissions testing) requirement effective July 1, 2023, ending testing in the Treasure Valley.
registrationFeeRange: $69 at 1 or 2 years, $57 at 3 to 6 years, or $45 at 7 or more years
registrationNotes: The $14 title fee is the state base. Counties add a title administrative fee (from $0 to $18.75) and a registration administrative fee. An electric vehicle pays an additional $140 a year and a plug-in hybrid $75.
lemonArbitration: Idaho has no state-run arbitration board. Under Idaho Code § 48-906, each manufacturer doing business in Idaho must operate or join an informal dispute settlement program located in the state, and a consumer generally must use it before suing for a refund or replacement. Its decision is nonbinding unless the parties agree otherwise, and either side can remove it to district court within 30 days.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $140 a year under Idaho Code § 49-457.

name: Illinois
description: Illinois requires 25/50/20 liability coverage plus uninsured motorist coverage, and requires emissions testing in the Chicago and Metro East St. Louis areas. Its lemon law covers the first year or 12,000 miles, and the Illinois EPA offers a rebate for buying an electric vehicle.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Illinois sets its own lemon-law period in 815 ILCS 380/2 and 380/3: one year or 12,000 miles after delivery, whichever comes first. Four repairs of the same problem that still exists, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption inside that period. The manufacturer must have received direct written notice from the buyer, or from someone acting for the buyer. It also needs a chance to correct the defect before the presumption applies.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required for most gasoline vehicles registered in Cook, DuPage, and Lake counties, and in designated parts of Kane, Kendall, McHenry, Will, Madison, Monroe, and St. Clair counties, under the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Law of 2005. Most 1996 and newer gasoline passenger vehicles are tested after they are four years old, on the biennial schedule that matches the license-plate year. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: The Illinois EPA EV rebate cycle runs August 1 to December 31, 2026: $2,000, or $4,000 for low-income applicants, and $1,500 for an electric motorcycle. The vehicle must be all-electric, sell for $80,000 or less, and be bought from an Illinois-licensed dealer, and applications must be postmarked within 180 days of purchase.
registrationFeeRange: $151 for most passenger vehicles
registrationNotes: Registration is annual and expires at the end of a month. An electric vehicle pays $251 a year ($151 plus a $100 fee in lieu of motor fuel tax). New residents have 30 days to title and register.
lemonArbitration: Illinois has no state lemon-law board. Under 815 ILCS 380/4, if the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure that substantially complies with 16 CFR part 703 and the consumer was given written notice of it, the consumer must use it before the refund-or-replace remedy applies. A dissatisfied consumer can then sue, and the decision is admissible. Direct written notice to the manufacturer under 815 ILCS 380/3(h) is also required before the repair presumption applies.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $100 a year. Annual renewal of that plate is listed at $251.

name: Indiana
description: Indiana requires 25/50/25 liability insurance, and its lemon law covers cars and light trucks for 18 months or 18,000 miles. Vehicles registered in Lake and Porter counties need emissions tests every two years, and out-of-state vehicles get a VIN inspection when they are first titled in Indiana.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Indiana calls the coverage a term of protection under Ind. Code §§ 24-5-13-7, 24-5-13-8, and 24-5-13-15. It ends at the earlier of 18 months or 18,000 miles, and the buyer has to report the problem before that term runs out. Four repairs that leave the problem in place, or 30 business days out of service with the problem still there, counts as a reasonable number of attempts. If the manufacturer made the disclosure in § 24-5-13-9, the buyer notifies the manufacturer of the claim first.
emissionsDetails: Vehicles registered in Lake and Porter counties need a Clean Air Car Check emissions test and tampering inspection every two years if they were built after 1975 and have a GVWR of 9,000 pounds or less. The four newest model years and antique vehicles are exempt. Vehicles are tested in years matching their model year (odd or even).
registrationFeeRange: $21.35 plus excise tax
registrationNotes: Registration is $21.35 a year plus an excise tax based on the vehicle's MSRP class and age, and some counties and cities add an excise or wheel tax. Title is $15, and a $30 late penalty applies after 45 days (60 days for new residents). A transfer or replacement plate is $9.50, and personalized plates are $45. Supplemental fees are $242 for EVs and $81 for hybrids.
lemonArbitration: Indiana has no state arbitration board. Under Ind. Code § 24-5-13-19, if the manufacturer has an informal dispute procedure certified by the Attorney General and gave the buyer written notice of it, the buyer must use it before suing. If the manufacturer made the disclosure in § 24-5-13-9, the buyer must also notify the manufacturer in writing first. Suit must be filed within two years of first reporting the defect, tolled during the dispute procedure.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: The BMV fee chart (revised 1/1/2026) lists a $242 electric-vehicle supplemental fee and an $81 hybrid supplemental fee under Ind. Code § 9-18.1-5-12. The fees are adjusted annually.

name: Iowa
description: Iowa requires 20/40/15 liability insurance plus uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage unless you reject it in writing. Its lemon law covers new vehicles for the warranty term, two years or 24,000 miles. Annual registration is based on value and weight, and the fee drops as the vehicle ages.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Iowa's lemon law, Iowa Code §§ 322G.2 and 322G.4, uses the written warranty, two years, or 24,000 miles, whichever expires first, and it counts calendar days. The presumption is three exams or repairs of the same problem plus a final attempt if one is undertaken, one exam or repair of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury plus that final attempt, or 30 days out of service. You can send written notice after 20 cumulative days out of service, after three attempts, or after one attempt on a dangerous defect. The manufacturer then has a final chance to conform the car, including 10 cumulative out-of-service days after the 20-day notice.
registrationFeeRange: 1% of value plus 40 cents per 100 pounds
registrationNotes: The annual fee is 1% of value plus 40 cents per 100 pounds. The value portion drops to 75% after seven model years and 50% after nine, with a $50 minimum, and the fee is a flat $50 at 12 model years or older. A one-time fee for new registration of $10 plus 5% of the purchase price applies when the vehicle is first registered to you. New residents have 30 days to title and register. Late renewals add 5% a month.
lemonArbitration: If the manufacturer has a program certified by the Attorney General and told the buyer how to file, the buyer must use it before claiming a refund or replacement (Iowa Code § 322G.6). Certified programs are free and must decide within 60 days. If a program misses its deadline, or there is no certified program and the final-repair notice was sent, the consumer may sue in district court within one year after the lemon law rights period ends (§ 322G.8).
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Iowa Code § 321.116 adds $130 a year for a battery-electric vehicle and $65 for a plug-in hybrid. Iowa DOT lists $9 for an electric or plug-in hybrid motorcycle.

name: Kansas
description: Kansas requires liability insurance with personal injury protection and uninsured motorist coverage, and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The Department of Revenue says the state has no safety or emissions inspection program. A VIN inspection applies when a vehicle is titled from another state.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage / personal injury protection (PIP) required, including $4,500 medical / uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage required at no less than 25/50
lemonLawSummary: Kansas applies Kan. Stat. Ann. § 50-645 during the express warranty or the first year after delivery, whichever ends sooner, and the statute sets no mileage limit. Four repairs of the same problem, 30 calendar days out of service, or ten attempts on any problems that substantially impair use and value, is the presumption. Those counts matter once the manufacturer has actual notice of the trouble. Get that notice to the manufacturer while the warranty or the one-year period is still open.
emissionsDetails: The Kansas Highway Patrol says the state does not require emissions testing, and Johnson County tells vehicle owners the same thing.
safetyInspectionDetails: The Kansas Department of Revenue says Kansas does not have a safety or emissions inspection requirement or program. A $20 VIN inspection by the Highway Patrol, or a designee, is required before titling a vehicle that comes in on an out-of-state title. Rebuilt salvage vehicles have a separate $25 inspection.
registrationFeeRange: $30 at 4,500 lb or less, or $40 above that weight
registrationNotes: Personal property tax is also assessed on vehicles. Kansas statute 8-143 lists $70 for an electric hybrid, $100 for a plug-in electric hybrid and $165 for an all-electric vehicle. New residents must title and register within 90 days, and buyers should apply within 60 days of purchase to avoid a penalty.
lemonArbitration: Kansas has no state-run arbitration board. Under Kan. Stat. Ann. § 50-645(e), if the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure that complies with 16 CFR part 703, the consumer must use it before seeking a refund or replacement under the statute. The Attorney General enforces the law.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An all-electric passenger vehicle is registered at $165 under Kansas statute 8-143.

name: Kentucky
description: Kentucky requires liability insurance with basic personal injury protection under its no-fault law, and has a lemon law for new vehicles. A 6% motor vehicle usage tax is collected when a vehicle is transferred or first registered in the state.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage, or a $60,000 single limit / $10,000 basic personal injury protection (PIP) / uninsured motorist coverage at the minimum bodily injury limits unless rejected in writing
lemonLawSummary: Kentucky's window under Ky. Rev. Stat. § 367.842 is the first 12 months or 12,000 miles, whichever arrives first. The presumption looks at that same defect: four repair attempts, or 30 calendar days the car is out of service because of it. When a reasonable number of attempts still leaves the car unrepaired, the buyer puts the problem in writing to the manufacturer.
emissionsDetails: Jefferson County's vehicle emissions testing program, run by the Louisville air pollution control district, ended by November 1, 2003, under KRS 77.320.
safetyInspectionDetails: Vehicles brought into Kentucky from another state need a sheriff's inspection before titling. Fees are set by county; Logan County lists $5.
registrationNotes: The state registration fee under KRS 186.050 is $11.50; Logan County's clerk lists $21 for a yearly renewal. A 6 percent usage tax applies when ownership transfers or a vehicle is first registered in Kentucky. New residents must apply within 15 days under KRS 186.020.
lemonArbitration: Under Ky. Rev. Stat. § 367.842(4), refund or replacement disputes must first go through the manufacturer's informal dispute resolution system under KRS 367.860 to 367.870 or 16 CFR part 703 before court. KRS 367.865 requires that system to be free to the buyer and available for disputes in the first two years or 25,000 miles.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Vehicles with plug-in charging capability pay an electric vehicle ownership fee under KRS 138.475 on top of registration. The base is $120, adjusted annually; the AFDC lists $126 for 2025.

name: Louisiana
description: Louisiana requires 15/30/25 liability insurance, and under R.S. 32:866 uninsured owners cannot recover the first $100,000 of bodily injury or property damage. It has a lemon law for new vehicles, an emissions program in five Baton Rouge-area parishes, and a yearly road usage fee for electric and hybrid vehicles. Act 701 of 2026 ends inspection stickers for personal vehicles outside those parishes on January 1, 2027.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: La. Rev. Stat. § 51:1943 gives the manufacturer the warranty period or one year after delivery, and the presumption uses the date that arrives first. The section does not cut the period off by mileage. Four repairs of the same problem, or 45 calendar days out of service, is the presumption, and § 51:1944 uses those same numbers for the refund or replacement. If the manufacturer misses the response or repair time in § 51:1943(A), it loses the right to a final attempt.
emissionsDetails: LDEQ emissions testing applies to gasoline vehicles of 10,000 lbs GVWR or less registered in Ascension, East Baton Rouge, Iberville, Livingston, and West Baton Rouge parishes: anti-tampering and gas-cap checks, plus OBD II for 1996 and newer. The inspection fee in these parishes is $18 for the combined safety and emissions inspection. Act 701 of 2026 takes effect in these parishes only if EPA approves the state plan amendments.
safetyInspectionDetails: Act 701 of 2026 prohibits inspection-certificate citations from June 30, 2026 to January 1, 2027. For personal non-commercial vehicles the inspection requirement ends January 1, 2027, except in the five Baton Rouge-area I/M parishes, where it takes effect only when EPA approves the State Implementation Plan amendments. Commercial and student transportation vehicles remain subject to inspection.
registrationFeeRange: 0.1% of vehicle value per year, sold in 2-year increments ($20 minimum)
registrationNotes: Automobile plates are sold for two years at 0.1 percent of value per year, with a minimum value of $10,000 ($20 minimum). Title $68.50, handling fee $8, lien recording $15 (UCC-1) or $10, and a local fee of up to $6. Electric vehicles pay a $110 and hybrids a $60 yearly road usage fee under R.S. 32:461.
lemonArbitration: Louisiana has no state lemon-law arbitration program. Under La. Rev. Stat. § 51:1944(D), if the manufacturer has an informal dispute procedure that substantially complies with 16 CFR part 703, the consumer must use it before the refund or replacement provisions apply. Suit must be filed within three years of purchase or one year after the warranty ends, whichever is longer.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: R.S. 32:461 road usage fee: $110 per year for electric vehicles and $60 per year for hybrids (prorated by month). OMV mails notices April 1 and May 1 for the prior calendar year; payment is due June 30.

name: Maine
description: Maine requires 50/100/25 liability insurance plus $2,000 medical payments and $500 towing coverage, and an annual safety inspection, with an enhanced emissions inspection in Cumberland County. The Maine Lemon Law includes free state-certified arbitration run by the Attorney General, and Efficiency Maine offers income-qualified rebates on electric vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage, plus $2,000 medical payments and $500 towing and storage (29-A M.R.S. § 1605); uninsured vehicle coverage is also required (24-A M.R.S. § 2902)
lemonLawSummary: Maine's repair duty in Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 10, § 1163 runs during the express warranties, three years, or 18,000 miles, whichever comes first. Three repairs of the same problem, one repair of a serious brake or steering failure, or 15 business days out of service, is the presumption. Write the manufacturer that you want a refund or a replacement. It then has a final repair chance during the seven business days after it receives the letter, and that letter can go out after a single brake or steering failure.
emissionsDetails: Vehicles registered in Cumberland County need an annual enhanced inspection under 29-A M.R.S. § 1751: fuel cap test on 1974 and newer gasoline vehicles and an on-board diagnostics check on 1996 and newer. Maine has adopted California vehicle emissions standards (DEP Chapter 127).
safetyInspectionDetails: Maine requires an annual inspection under 29-A M.R.S. § 1751. The station may charge no more than $12.50 for a standard inspection. A Cumberland County enhanced inspection may not exceed $15.50 for a pre-1996 vehicle or $18.50 for a 1996 or newer vehicle. The fee is due whether the vehicle passes or not.
evIncentiveDetails: Efficiency Maine offers income-qualified rebates on all-electric vehicles paired with an off-peak charger: $7,000 new / $3,000 used for low-income buyers and $5,000 new / $2,000 used for moderate-income buyers. A $1,000 enhancement ran through September 30, 2026. Plug-in hybrids and leases are not eligible.
registrationFeeRange: $35 per year for a passenger vehicle
registrationNotes: Annual excise tax is paid to the town before registration, based on MSRP and age (24 mills in year 1 down to 4 mills from year 6). Passenger registration is $35 a year. Title application $33 for vehicles 25 model years old or newer; 5.5% sales tax on private or out-of-state purchases. New residents have 30 days to register. Vanity plates are an extra $25.
lemonArbitration: Manufacturers must submit to state-certified arbitration under Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 10, § 1169 when the consumer applies within three years of original delivery or during the express warranty, whichever ends first, and the Attorney General accepts the file. The written finding is due within 45 days, and an appeal is a new trial in the Superior Court of the county where the vehicle was sold.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Maryland
description: Maryland requires 30/60/15 liability coverage plus PIP and uninsured motorist coverage, a one-time safety inspection before a used vehicle is titled, and emissions testing every two years in 13 counties and Baltimore City. The state lemon law covers the first 18,000 miles or 24 months, and an excise tax credit of up to $3,000 is available for qualifying EVs.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage, plus $2,500 personal injury protection (waivable in writing) and uninsured motorist coverage (Transp. § 17-103)
lemonLawSummary: Maryland's lemon law is Md. Code, Com. Law §§ 14-1501 and 14-1502. For this statute the manufacturer's warranty period is the earlier of 18,000 miles or 24 months after delivery. The presumption is four repairs of the same problem, 30 or more days out of service, or one repair of a brake or steering failure that still will not pass the state safety inspection after the manufacturer had a chance to cure. Report the problem by certified mail, return receipt requested, and the manufacturer is supposed to finish the corrections within 30 days of getting that letter.
emissionsDetails: Eligible vehicles in the VEIP counties are tested every two years. A qualifying new vehicle is first tested 72 months from the model year. The test fee is $30, or $26 at a self-serve kiosk. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Under Transp. § 23-107, a used vehicle (other than a historic vehicle) needs a valid Maryland Safety Inspection certificate before it is titled and registered. The certificate is valid for 90 days. Transfers between spouses, parent and child, or co-owners are among those exempt.
evIncentiveDetails: Excise tax credit under Transp. § 13-815: $3,000 for a new zero-emission or fuel cell vehicle with a base price of $50,000 or less, titled from July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2027; $2,000 for 3-wheeled and $1,000 for 2-wheeled electric motorcycles. Subject to funding; the MVA reported $2.2 million available for FY2027 on October 1, 2026.
registrationNotes: Amounts include the $40 EMS surcharge and can be paid for 1, 2 or 3 years. Title fee $200 (Transp. § 13-802). Excise tax 6.5% of price or book value, minimum $41.60; new residents within 60 days get credit for tax paid to the prior state. Vanity plates $50.
lemonArbitration: Maryland has no state arbitration board. A consumer may use a manufacturer program that complies with 16 CFR Part 703 (Com. Law § 14-1502(i)), and its decision binds only the manufacturer. The Attorney General Consumer Protection Division takes lemon law complaints and helps negotiate with manufacturers. Suits must be filed within 3 years of delivery.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A battery-electric vehicle pays a $125 annual surcharge. A plug-in hybrid pays $100 a year.

name: Massachusetts
description: Massachusetts requires an annual safety inspection, plus an emissions test for most vehicles under 15 years old. A vehicle that runs only on electricity skips the emissions portion. Minimum liability limits rose to 25/50/30 for policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2025.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $30,000 property damage, plus $8,000 PIP and 25/50 uninsured motorist bodily injury (policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2025)
lemonLawSummary: Massachusetts calls the coverage a term of protection of one year or 15,000 miles in Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 90, § 7N 1/2, and a business day is a day the authorized dealers' service departments are normally open. Three repairs of the same problem that continues or comes back, or 15 business days out of service, is a reasonable number of attempts. The manufacturer gets one more chance to cure, and that extra chance cannot run longer than seven business days. The buyer does not have to notify the manufacturer directly before using the state's certified new-car arbitration.
emissionsDetails: A light-duty nondiesel vehicle is exempt when its model year is earlier than 1996 or the vehicle is 15 or more model years old. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test. The vehicle still needs the annual safety inspection.
safetyInspectionDetails: Massachusetts requires an annual safety inspection for every registered vehicle. The inspection is $35 for most vehicles. A vehicle operated only on electricity still needs the safety inspection.
evIncentiveDetails: MOR-EV pays $3,500 for an eligible new EV with a total MSRP up to $55,000 and $3,500 for an income-qualified used EV priced up to $40,000, plus a $1,500 MOR-EV+ adder for participants in listed assistance programs and a $1,000 trade-in rebate (mor-ev.org).
registrationFeeRange: $60 for most passenger vehicles
registrationNotes: Registration is $60 for two years and a title is $75. A 6.25 percent sales tax applies, the vehicle must be inspected within 7 days of registration, and cities and towns bill an annual excise of $25 per $1,000 of value.
usedCarLemonLaw: The Massachusetts used-vehicle warranty law is General Laws chapter 90, section 7N 1/4. If a dealer will not refund the car, the buyer can request state-certified used-car arbitration from the Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation within six months of taking delivery.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
lemonArbitration: Under M.G.L. c. 90, § 7N½, every manufacturer must take part in the state-certified arbitration program run by the Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation if the consumer asks within 18 months of original delivery. The arbitrator's fee is $300, and the written decision is due within 45 days after the director receives the request.

name: Michigan
description: Michigan is a no-fault insurance state. Policies must carry personal injury protection, property protection insurance and residual liability, and drivers choose among six PIP medical levels: unlimited, $500,000, $250,000, $250,000 with exclusions, $50,000 for Medicaid enrollees, or none for people with Medicare Parts A and B. Under the no-fault law, PPI covers up to $1 million of damage your car causes in Michigan to buildings, fences and properly parked vehicles that belong to others. The state does not require a safety or emissions inspection to register a vehicle.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 per accident (the default is 250/500 unless you sign the DIFS limits form) / $10,000 property damage in another state / $1 million property protection insurance in Michigan / PIP with a chosen medical level
lemonLawSummary: Michigan's lemon law, Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 257.1402 and 257.1403, asks the owner to report the defect during the express warranty or within one year of delivery, whichever is earlier, and it sets no mileage cap. The presumption is four repairs of the same defect within two years of the first repair attempt, or 30 days out of service during the warranty or that first year. After the third repair, send written notice by return receipt; the manufacturer then has five business days to repair. On the days-out path, written notice goes out after 25 days in the shop, and the manufacturer again has five business days.
evIncentiveDetails: Michigan has no state rebate or tax credit for buying an EV. EGLE Charge Up Michigan grants fund DC fast chargers for site hosts.
registrationFeeRange: Based on the vehicle's list price
registrationNotes: The registration tax for a 1984 or newer passenger vehicle is based on list price under MCL 257.801 ($36 at $6,000 or less, rising $6 per $1,000) and falls to 90 percent in the second and third years. Title transfer is $15 within 15 days of sale, plus 6 percent sales tax on the greater of price or fair market value.
lemonArbitration: Michigan has no state lemon-law arbitrator. After the return-receipt notice in Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 257.1402 and 257.1403, the manufacturer gets five business days to repair. If the car is still defective and the manufacturer has a qualifying informal dispute program, MCL 257.1405 requires you to use it before relying on the act in court.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A vehicle that runs only on electricity and weighs 8,000 pounds or less has a statutory add-on of $100. The add-on rises with the gasoline tax above 19 cents a gallon under MCL 257.801.

name: Minnesota
description: Minnesota is a no-fault state that requires PIP, liability, and uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage. Its lemon law covers new vehicles, and registration tax is based on MSRP and vehicle age.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $40,000 PIP ($20,000 medical, $20,000 non-medical) / $25,000/$50,000 uninsured and underinsured motorist
lemonLawSummary: Minn. Stat. § 325F.665 places the presumption in the express warranty or in the two years after delivery, and the date that comes first ends it. Miles do not shorten that window. A problem first reported while the warranty was still running can still support a refund or replacement from attempts made within three years of delivery. The presumption is four repairs, 30 business days out of service, or a single repair of a complete brake or steering failure that is likely to cause death or serious injury, and the four-repair and 30-day routes need written notice plus a chance to cure.
emissionsDetails: Minnesota's Twin Cities auto emissions inspection program ended on March 1, 2000, when the Legislature repealed it. The state does not require an emissions test to register a vehicle.
evIncentiveDetails: Minnesota Department of Commerce says all funds for the 2023 state EV rebate ($2,500 new, $600 used) have been claimed and it is not taking new applications.
registrationFeeRange: $10 plus 1.575 percent of MSRP
registrationNotes: The percentage applies to a vehicle first registered in Minnesota on or after November 16, 2020. The share of MSRP falls with age. From the 11th year the amount added to the base is $20. All-electric vehicles add a surcharge of at least $150 (2026 to mid-2027), and plug-in hybrids at least $75. The motor vehicle sales tax is 6.875%.
usedCarLemonLaw: Minnesota's used-car warranty is Minn. Stat. § 325F.662. The Attorney General's handbook says a dealer must cover most used cars and small trucks sold to a Minnesota buyer for 60 days or 2,500 miles under 36,000 miles, 30 days or 1,000 miles from 36,000 to under 75,000 miles, and 15 days or 500 miles from 75,000 to under 200,000 miles. A private-party sale is outside that statute, and the handbook does not describe a state arbitration program for it.
lemonArbitration: Under Minn. Stat. § 325F.665, subd. 6, each manufacturer must run or join an informal dispute mechanism in Minnesota that complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703, and a consumer must use it before suing for a refund or replacement. The decision is nonbinding, and either side may remove it to district court.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An all-electric vehicle pays a surcharge of the greater of 0.5% of age-adjusted MSRP or $150 for periods starting January 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 ($100 from July 1, 2027). Plug-in hybrids pay 0.25% or a $75 minimum ($50 from July 1, 2027).

name: Mississippi
description: Mississippi requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles and has a lemon law for new vehicle purchases. The state does not require emissions testing or annual safety inspections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Miss. Code Ann. § 63-17-159 keeps the repair presumption inside the express warranty or the first year after delivery, whichever finishes sooner. The section does not add a mileage limit. Substantially the same problem repaired three times, or 15 working days in the shop for that problem, is enough, and routine maintenance is not part of the 15 days. Write the manufacturer before you rely on the section; once the car is at the shop the manufacturer names, that shop has ten working days to make it conform.
evIncentiveDetails: Mississippi offers no state purchase rebate or tax credit for EVs. The state AFV revolving loan program for school districts and cities covers propane and natural gas.
registrationFeeRange: $12.75 to renew or $14 for a first registration
registrationNotes: A passenger vehicle also pays the $15 highway privilege tax (Miss. Code Ann. § 27-19-5). Local ad valorem tax is charged on 30% of MSRP, depreciated over 10 years, less the Legislative Tag Credit. Sales tax is 5% of the net price, and new residents have 30 days to register.
lemonArbitration: Mississippi runs no state lemon-law arbitration board. Under Miss. Code Ann. § 63-17-163, if the manufacturer has an informal dispute procedure that complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703 and told you about it, you must use it before claiming a refund or replacement. A suit must be filed within 90 days of the panel's final action.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Under Miss. Code Ann. §§ 27-19-21 and 27-19-23, all-electric vehicles pay an annual fee that started at $150, and plug-in hybrids and hybrids one that started at $75. Since July 1, 2021, the Department of Revenue has adjusted both every July 1 for CPI.

name: Missouri
description: Missouri requires liability and uninsured motorist coverage. Safety inspections are biennial, with an exemption for vehicles in their first ten model years with fewer than 150,000 miles. Emissions testing applies in the St. Louis area and not in Kansas City. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage / $25,000/$50,000 uninsured motorist
lemonLawSummary: Under Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 407.565 and 407.571, the clock runs for the express warranty or for one year after delivery, and the period that ends first controls. There is no mileage cutoff in that test. The same problem repaired four times, or the car held for repair for 30 working days, meets the presumption, and days spent on ordinary maintenance stay out of the count. Tell the manufacturer or its agent about the problem before that window closes.
emissionsDetails: The Gateway Vehicle Inspection Program tests gasoline vehicles from model year 1996 and diesel vehicles from model year 1997, at or under 8,500 pounds, that are registered in St. Louis City or in St. Louis, St. Charles, or Jefferson County. Franklin County residents have been exempt since July 1, 2022. Kansas City is not in the program. The state cap on the emissions inspection fee is $24. Even model years are tested in even calendar years, and odd model years in odd calendar years. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: RSMo § 307.350 requires a biennial safety inspection, in the even calendar year for an even model year and in the odd calendar year for an odd model year, and also when ownership changes. A vehicle is exempt for the first ten model years if it has fewer than 150,000 miles, other than a prior salvage vehicle right after it is rebuilt. The certificate is generally valid for 60 days. The Department of Revenue said on January 6, 2026, that these rules had not changed.
evIncentiveDetails: No state EV purchase rebate or tax credit is listed. Vehicles powered only by electricity are exempt from emissions inspection (RSMo § 643.315).
registrationFeeRange: $18.25 - $51.25 based on horsepower
registrationNotes: A $9 processing fee is added to a one-year registration ($18 for two years). Title is $8.50 plus a $9 processing fee, due within 30 days of purchase. Sales tax is 4.225% state plus local.
lemonArbitration: Missouri has no state lemon-law arbitration board. Under Mo. Rev. Stat. § 407.575, a consumer must first use a manufacturer's informal dispute procedure that complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703, if one exists. Written notice under § 407.573 gives the manufacturer a final ten calendar days to repair.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle registers in the lowest passenger bracket ($18.25 a year) and must also carry an annual special fuel decal: $150 for an EV and $75 for a 2018-or-newer plug-in hybrid in 2026, plus a $9 processing fee (RSMo § 142.869).

name: Montana
description: Montana requires 25/50/20 liability insurance and does not require emissions testing or safety inspections. Light-vehicle registration fees are based on vehicle age, and counties may add a local option tax. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles with a state-run arbitration program.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Montana defines the warranty period in Mont. Code Ann. §§ 61-4-501 and 61-4-504 as two years or 18,000 miles, whichever is earlier. The presumption is four repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service after the manufacturer, its agent, or a dealer was notified. Send written notice to the manufacturer or its agent while the warranty period is still open. The manufacturer has to tell the buyer that written notice is required, and the presumption is not used against a manufacturer that never received that notice and a chance to cure.
registrationFeeRange: $217 at 0 to 4 years, $87 at 5 to 10 years, or $28 at 11 years or older
registrationNotes: A county option tax of up to 0.7% of depreciated MSRP may be added, along with a $9 state parks fee (opt-out allowed) and other fees. Vehicles 11 years or older can be permanently registered.
lemonArbitration: The Montana Department of Justice provides arbitration under Mont. Code Ann. § 61-4-515 when the manufacturer has no certified dispute program. The consumer pays a $100 filing fee and the manufacturer $750, and the arbitrator decides within 60 days. If the manufacturer has a certified program, the consumer must use it first (§ 61-4-507).
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An annual fee is added at registration under Mont. Code Ann. § 61-3-572: $130 for a class 1 EV (under 6,000 lbs) or $70 for a class 1 plug-in hybrid, rising by weight class to $1,100 and $700.

name: Nebraska
description: Nebraska requires 25/50/25 liability insurance plus uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage. The state does not require emissions testing, charges an annual motor vehicle tax based on MSRP and age, and has a lemon law for new vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage, plus $25,000/$50,000 uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage
lemonLawSummary: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-2704 times the presumption to the express warranty or to one year after delivery, and the earlier of those two dates ends it. The statute does not set a mileage limit. The car meets the test after four repairs of the same problem or after 40 days out of service. That test is available only once the manufacturer has notice by certified mail and a chance to cure.
registrationFeeRange: $15 plus motor vehicle tax
registrationNotes: The motor vehicle tax is based on MSRP and age and ends after the 13th year. A motor vehicle fee, $2/$1.50/$0.50 state fees and a $1.50 county fee are added. Sales tax is 5.5% state plus up to 2.5% local, due within 30 days of purchase.
lemonArbitration: Nebraska has no state-run lemon-law arbitration board. Under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-2705, if a manufacturer has an informal dispute procedure certified by the Director of Motor Vehicles, the consumer must use it before claiming a refund or replacement. A prevailing consumer in court is awarded reasonable attorney fees (§ 60-2707).
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric or hydrogen passenger vehicle pays a $150 alternative-fuel fee. A plug-in electric passenger vehicle pays $75.

name: Nevada
description: Nevada requires liability insurance and annual emissions testing in the urban areas of Clark and Washoe counties. Its lemon law covers new vehicles under NRS 597.600 to 597.688, and Lemon Law Buyback titles must be disclosed to later buyers.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Nevada asks the buyer to report the problem in writing under NRS 597.610 before the express warranty ends or one year after delivery to the original buyer, whichever is earlier. NRS 597.630 then presumes enough attempts after four repairs of the same problem or 30 calendar days out of service. The 30-day count can run longer when the needed repair is delayed for reasons outside the manufacturer's or dealer's control.
emissionsDetails: Qualifying gasoline vehicles based in urban Clark County or Washoe County need an annual test beginning with the fourth registration. The 2026 maximum for a light-duty gasoline test is $75.50 in Clark County and $71.50 in Washoe County. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationFeeRange: $33 plus governmental services tax
registrationNotes: The Governmental Services Tax is 4% of a depreciated valuation set at 35% of original MSRP, with a $16 minimum. Clark and Churchill counties add a Supplemental GST. Private-party sales and gifts are not subject to sales tax.
lemonArbitration: NRS 597.600 to 597.688 do not set up a state arbitration program. If the manufacturer has an informal dispute procedure that substantially complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703, NRS 597.620 requires the buyer to use it before suing under NRS 597.630.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: New Hampshire
description: New Hampshire does not require drivers to carry auto insurance, though they remain financially responsible for damages. The DMV's February 13, 2026 guidance suspends the vehicle inspection program until further notice.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage / $1,000 medical payments (RSA 264:16) / uninsured motorist coverage at the liability limits (RSA 264:15). Insurance is not mandatory in New Hampshire, but a policy you carry must meet these minimums.
lemonLawSummary: New Hampshire's presumption in RSA 357-D:3, VII is measured during the express warranty. Three repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service, meets the presumption, counting a business day as a day those dealers normally keep a service department open. Repair attempts should be on written repair orders, generally at the same dealer, and a car the owner can use for a major part of the day is not out of service. After the third repair or after those 30 business days, RSA 357-D:4 requires written notice to the manufacturer, which then gets one final chance to repair.
safetyInspectionDetails: The New Hampshire DMV's February 13, 2026 guidance says the vehicle inspection program is suspended until further notice. Stations are not issuing state inspection stickers, and an annual inspection is not required while that suspension stands. Drivers remain responsible for the equipment rules in RSA 266. OBD emissions testing was part of that inspection. The status can change.
registrationFeeRange: $42 up to 3,000 lb, $48 from 3,001 to 5,000 lb, or $66 from 5,001 to 8,000 lb
registrationNotes: The town or city permit fee under RSA 261:153 runs from 18 mills per dollar of list price for a current model year vehicle down to 3 mills, with a $5 minimum. The title fee rose from $25 to $35 on January 1, 2026 (RSA 261:20).
lemonArbitration: The New Hampshire New Motor Vehicle Arbitration Board is attached to the Division of Motor Vehicles under RSA 357-D. A buyer who already chose the manufacturer's dispute program cannot also file with that board.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: RSA 261:141-c adds an annual surcharge of $100 for a battery electric vehicle and $50 for a plug-in hybrid. From January 1, 2027, the BEV surcharge is set by GVWR: $0 up to 1,000 lb, $50 from 1,001 to 3,000 lb, $100 from 3,001 to 8,000 lb, and $150 over 8,000 lb; PHEVs stay at $50.

name: New Jersey
description: New Jersey is a no-fault state. A Standard Policy needs at least 35/70/25 liability plus PIP, and the lower-cost Basic Policy is a legal alternative. Passenger vehicles take an emissions inspection every two years after a five-year new-car decal, and the New Car Lemon Law has a state hearing program run by the Division of Consumer Affairs.
insuranceMinimumDetail: Standard Policy: $35,000 bodily injury per person / $70,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage / PIP of at least $15,000, up to $250,000 for certain injuries. The Basic Policy under N.J.S.A. 39:6A-3.1 is also legal. It carries $15,000 PIP, $5,000 property damage and no bodily injury liability unless you add the optional $10,000.
lemonLawSummary: New Jersey's lemon law, N.J.S.A. 56:12-33, uses the first 24,000 miles or two years, and a motorhome uses 45 calendar days out of service where a passenger car uses 20. Three repairs of substantially the same problem, that days-out total, or one exam of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, is the presumption. It applies only after the manufacturer received certified-mail notice, return receipt requested, and had one chance to repair within 10 calendar days. That letter may go out after two repairs, after the car has been out 20 calendar days (45 for a motorhome), or after one exam of a serious safety problem.
emissionsDetails: New Jersey requires biennial emissions inspections for most vehicles 5+ model years old. Testing is performed at state Motor Vehicle Commission inspection stations at no charge. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Charge Up New Jersey takes $1,500 off a new battery-electric vehicle with an MSRP up to $55,000 at the dealer, or $4,000 total for income-qualified Charge Up+ applicants who prequalify. A home Level 2 charger can get up to $250. Plug-in hybrids don't qualify.
registrationFeeRange: $46.50 or $59 under 3,500 lb, and $71.50 or $84 above 3,500 lb
registrationNotes: The lower amount in each pair is for a model older than two years. The higher amount is for a model within two years.
usedCarLemonLaw: New Jersey's used-car lemon law is N.J.S.A. 56:8-67 and the sections that follow. The Division of Consumer Affairs Lemon Law Unit reviews a used-car application and, when it qualifies, the dispute goes to a hearing with the Office of Administrative Law.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A zero-emission vehicle pays an added annual fee of $250 beginning July 1, 2024. That fee rises by $10 a year for four years.
lemonArbitration: The Division of Consumer Affairs Lemon Law Unit accepts eligible applications for a $50 fee and refers them to the Office of Administrative Law for a hearing within 20 days. The Director's final decision binds both sides, subject to appeal. You can file in Superior Court instead.

name: New Mexico
description: New Mexico requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has emissions testing in the Albuquerque area and a lemon law covering new vehicle purchases.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: NMSA 1978 § 57-16A-3(C) covers a new vehicle for the express warranty or for the year after delivery, and the presumption follows the date that arrives first. Miles are not a separate cutoff. Four repairs that leave the same problem uncorrected, or 30 business days the car sits with the manufacturer, an agent, or a dealer, meets the test, not counting routine maintenance. Direct written notice and a chance to cure have to come first, and the manufacturer must say so in the warranty or in a separate notice.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing applies to vehicles registered or commuting in Bernalillo County. Vehicles from 1991 and newer, up to 10,000 pounds, are tested every two years and at a change of ownership. A brand-new vehicle is exempt for four years after the first registration on the manufacturer certificate of origin. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: New Mexico's Clean Car Income Tax Credit pays $3,000 for a new electric vehicle and $2,500 for a new plug-in hybrid, fuel cell vehicle or used EV bought or leased from a New Mexico licensed dealer in tax years 2024 through 2026, with lower amounts through 2029. New vehicles must have a base MSRP of $55,000 or less, used vehicles a market value of $25,000 or less, and EMNRD must certify eligibility within a year of purchase.
registrationFeeRange: Based on shipping weight and years registered
registrationNotes: Chapter 4 of the 2026 laws set the twelve-month fees. After five years of registration the fees are $26.25, $38.75, and $56.25. Before that they are $33.75, $48.75, and $70. Each registration includes a $1.50 tire recycling fee.
lemonArbitration: The Motor Vehicle Quality Assurance Act doesn't create a state hearing program. If the manufacturer runs an informal dispute procedure that complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703, NMSA 1978 § 57-16A-6 requires the buyer to use it before seeking a refund or replacement. A lawsuit must be filed within 18 months of delivery, or within 90 days after the program's final action if that is later.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Starting January 1, 2027, NMSA 1978 § 66-6-6.4 adds an annual fee of $70 for electric vehicles and $35 for plug-in hybrids, rising to $80 and $40 in 2028 and $90 and $45 from 2029.

name: New York
description: New York requires no-fault insurance with $50,000 in personal injury protection, an annual safety inspection that includes an emissions check for applicable vehicles, and a new car lemon law covering the first 18,000 miles or two years.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $50,000 PIP (no-fault) required
lemonLawSummary: New York's general presumption in General Business Law § 198-a(d) covers the first 18,000 miles or two years. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the test for a car. During that period, report the problem to the manufacturer, its agent, or an authorized dealer, and the agent or dealer has seven days to forward written notice by certified mail. Motor homes in the same section follow a different path: certified-mail notice after two repairs or 21 days out of service, and the owner may proceed after three repairs or 30 days out, if the manufacturer gave prior written notice of that requirement.
emissionsDetails: Annual emissions testing is required statewide as part of the annual safety inspection for most vehicles 2+ model years old. OBD-II testing is used for 1996+ model year vehicles. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, tires, lights, glass, exhaust, and emissions. Cost varies by shop but is typically $10-$37.
evIncentiveDetails: NYSERDA's Drive Clean Rebate takes $500 to $2,000 off the purchase or lease of an eligible new EV at participating dealers, based on the model's MSRP and all-electric range. AFDC lists a state tax credit of 50% of charger costs up to $5,000 under Tax Law § 187-b.
registrationFeeRange: $26 - $140 based on weight
registrationNotes: The weight schedule is the two-year fee. New York City residents also pay a supplemental registration fee. Sales tax varies by county.
usedCarLemonLaw: New York's used-car lemon law is General Business Law § 198-b.
