The Attorney General says a qualifying dealer-warranty dispute can go to the New York State Used Car Lemon Law Arbitration Program, which the New York State Dispute Resolution Association administers, and a decision in that program binds the buyer and the dealer.
lemonArbitration: Under General Business Law § 198-a(k), a consumer can take a new-car dispute to the Attorney General's alternate arbitration program, and the manufacturer must take part. The New York State Dispute Resolution Association administers the hearings and lists a $250 filing fee that is refunded if the consumer wins. Under § 198-a(g), a consumer who skips a manufacturer's own dispute program can't claim a refund or replacement under subdivision (c), and the Bill of Rights notice describes the Attorney General's program as an alternative to it.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: North Carolina
description: North Carolina requires liability insurance and an annual safety inspection statewide. Emissions testing remains in 19 counties until EPA approves the end of that program.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $50,000 property damage for policies issued or renewed on or after July 1, 2025 (previously 30/60/25), plus uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage
lemonLawSummary: North Carolina allows a refund or replacement under N.C.G.S. § 20-351.3 for a defect that substantially impairs value and showed up no later than 24 months or 24,000 miles after delivery. The presumption in § 20-351.5 is four repairs of the same problem that still exists, or 20 business days out of service during any 12-month period of the warranty. Express warranties have to last at least one year or 12,000 miles, and the repair duty runs for one year or the express-warranty term, whichever is longer. Notify the manufacturer directly in writing and allow up to 15 calendar days to correct the problem, unless it never disclosed that written notice was required; § 20-351.7 also requires a separate 10-day written notice before you sue.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is part of the annual inspection in 19 counties. Session Law 2023-134 and Session Law 2026-41 end that emissions program after EPA approval, and the annual safety inspection remains statewide. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: North Carolina requires an annual safety inspection statewide for registered vehicles. The emissions portion, where it still applies, is limited to 19 counties and is separate from the statewide safety inspection.
registrationNotes: Registration and licensing are annual.
lemonArbitration: The New Motor Vehicles Warranties Act lets a manufacturer require an informal settlement procedure before a lawsuit if the procedure substantially complies with the Magnuson-Moss Warranty Act and the warranty says so clearly. Under N.C.G.S. § 20-351.7, the owner must also give the manufacturer written notice of intent to sue at least 10 days before filing.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A plug-in electric vehicle that uses no other power source pays an additional $214.50. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $107.25.

name: North Dakota
description: North Dakota requires liability insurance plus $30,000 of no-fault benefits per person, and its lemon law covers new passenger vehicles and light trucks. Annual registration fees depend on weight and the number of years the vehicle has been registered.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: N.D.C.C. § 51-07-19 measures repairs during the express warranty or during the year after delivery, and the shorter of those two periods is the one that counts. There is no mileage cap on that presumption. More than three repairs of the same problem, which means a fourth visit while the trouble is still present, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption. It does not run against the manufacturer until the manufacturer has had direct notice and a chance to cure.
registrationFeeRange: $49 - $274 based on weight and year
registrationNotes: The 2026 schedule uses weight and the year first registered, not the model year.
lemonArbitration: If the manufacturer runs or takes part in an informal dispute program that substantially complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703, N.D.C.C. § 51-07-18(3) requires the consumer to use it before claiming a refund or replacement, and an oral hearing must be held in the consumer's state. The Attorney General decides on application whether a program qualifies. A lawsuit must be filed within six months after the earlier of the warranty's expiration or 18 months after delivery.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $120 road-use fee. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $50.

name: Ohio
description: Ohio requires drivers to maintain proof of financial responsibility, usually a 25/50/25 liability policy, for every registered vehicle. E-Check emissions testing applies in seven northeast Ohio counties.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Ohio's lemon law, Ohio Rev. Code § 1345.73, uses the first year or 18,000 miles, whichever is earlier, the same window § 1345.72 uses for reporting a repair. Three repairs of substantially the same problem, 30 calendar days out of service, eight attempts to repair any problems, or one attempt at a problem likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, is enough if the problem continues or comes back. Report the nonconformity to the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer during that year or 18,000 miles.
emissionsDetails: E-Check applies in Cuyahoga, Geauga, Lake, Lorain, Medina, Portage, and Summit counties. Gasoline and diesel vehicles that are 6 to 25 years old, and non-plug-in hybrids that are 7 to 25 years old, are tested every two years at 10,000 pounds or less. An established Ohio resident gets one free passing test in 365 days. According to the Alternative Fuels Data Center, vehicles powered solely by electricity are exempt after a one-time verification inspection.
registrationFeeRange: $36 plus deputy and permissive tax
registrationNotes: The deputy registrar fee for one year is $8. County permissive tax cannot exceed $30. A replacement plate is $15 for one plate or $16.25 for two. A hybrid pays an additional $100 a year.
lemonArbitration: The Ohio Attorney General approves manufacturer arbitration programs under Ohio Rev. Code § 1345.77. A buyer must use an approved program before suing, and a civil action has to be filed within five years after delivery.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $200 a year. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $150 a year.

name: Oklahoma
description: Oklahoma requires 25/50/25 liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles up to 10,000 pounds, plus recreational vehicles. An excise tax of 3.25% of value is due when a vehicle changes hands or is first registered in the state.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: 15 O.S. § 901(D) places Oklahoma's presumption inside the express warranty or the year after delivery, and the period that ends first is the one that applies. Mileage is not part of that cutoff. The same problem repaired four times, or 30 business days in the shop, creates the presumption. Put the report in writing to the manufacturer during the warranty or that year; without that notice and a chance to cure, the presumption does not apply.
registrationFeeRange: Based on the year of registration
registrationNotes: The fee is $96 for registration years 1 through 4. It then steps down to $26 from year 17 on. The motor vehicle excise tax under 68 O.S. § 2103 is 3.25 percent of value for a new vehicle, and $20 on the first $1,500 of value plus 3.25 percent of the rest for a used one.
lemonArbitration: If the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure that complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703, 15 O.S. § 901(F) requires the consumer to use it before the refund and replacement provisions apply. The Attorney General's guide says no state agency enforces the lemon law, and a consumer who prevails in court recovers costs and reasonable attorney fees.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Under 68 O.S. § 6511, EVs pay an annual fee of $110 at 6,000 pounds GVWR or less and $158 from 6,001 to 10,000 pounds; plug-in hybrids pay $82 and $118. Heavier vehicles pay more.

name: Oregon
description: Oregon requires 25/50/20 liability insurance plus personal injury protection and uninsured motorist coverage, and registration fees depend on a vehicle's MPG rating. Its lemon law covers new passenger vehicles for two years or 24,000 miles, and DEQ emissions testing applies in the Portland and Medford areas.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Oregon's lemon law, ORS 646A.406, uses two years after delivery or 24,000 miles, whichever ends first. The presumption is three repairs plus a chance to cure, 30 calendar days out of service (60 for a motor home), or one repair plus a final attempt on a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, if the problem continues. Before the presumption is used, the manufacturer needs a direct letter about the defect and a chance to correct it.
emissionsDetails: Non-exempt passenger vehicles in the Portland and Medford areas are tested every two years. The DEQ test fee is $25 in Portland and $20 in Medford, and only after a passing result. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Oregon's Clean Vehicle Rebate covers purchases and leases from August 25 to November 4, 2026. DEQ said on October 17, 2026 that available funds were running low and that later applications may be waitlisted until spring 2027. The Standard Rebate is up to $2,000, and the income-qualified Charge Ahead Rebate is up to $7,500 for a new BEV.
registrationFeeRange: $126 at 0 to 19 MPG, $136 at 20 to 39 MPG, or $216 at 40 MPG or higher
registrationNotes: A new passenger vehicle with a manufacturer certificate of origin is registered for four years, and that registration fee is doubled. Multnomah County adds $112. Washington County and Clackamas County add $60.
lemonArbitration: If the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure that substantially complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703 and tells the consumer about it, ORS 646A.408 requires the consumer to use it before claiming a refund or replacement. The decision binds the manufacturer but not the consumer. A lawsuit must be filed within one year after the earlier of 24,000 miles or two years from delivery.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An all-electric passenger vehicle that is not enrolled in OReGO pays $376 for two years. The title fee for that vehicle is $192. The miles-per-gallon schedule does not apply.

name: Pennsylvania
description: Pennsylvania requires 15/30/5 liability insurance plus $5,000 in medical benefits, and drivers choose between limited and full tort. Vehicles need an annual safety inspection, and emission inspections apply in designated counties. The Clean Vehicles Program applies California emission standards to new cars and light trucks.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Pennsylvania's Automobile Lemon Law, the Act of March 28, 1984, P.L. 150, No. 28, covers a car for one year, 12,000 miles, or the warranty, whichever comes first. A motorcycle uses one year or the warranty, and the statute does not add a mileage cap for motorcycles. Three repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the presumption in section 6. When the car comes back to the same dealer a second time for the same problem, section 7 says the dealer notifies the manufacturer by certified mail within seven days.
emissionsDetails: Gasoline vehicles from model year 1975 and newer with a GVWR of 9,000 pounds or less that are registered in a designated I/M county or region need an annual emission inspection with the safety inspection (67 Pa. Code § 177.51). Current model year vehicles and vehicles driven less than 5,000 miles a year are exempt. The emission sticker has no state fee.
safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for every registered vehicle. The official inspection sticker fee is $12.
registrationNotes: Registration is $48 for one year or $96 for two, and some counties add a $5 Fee for Local Use. The Commonwealth sales tax is 6 percent, and Act 21 of 2026 requires vendors to collect Philadelphia's 2 percent and Allegheny County's 1 percent local sales taxes.
lemonLawCitation: Automobile Lemon Law, Act of Mar. 28, 1984, P.L. 150, No. 28, § 6
lemonArbitration: If the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure that complies with 16 CFR Part 703, section 9 of the Automobile Lemon Law requires the purchaser to use it before suing. The decision isn't binding on the purchaser, who can then bring a civil action in a court of common pleas and recover attorneys' fees and court costs.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Pennsylvania's 2026 Road User Charge is $250 a year for an EV and $63 for a plug-in hybrid, or $500 and $126 for a two-year registration, on top of the regular registration fee.

name: Rhode Island
description: Rhode Island requires 25/50/25 liability insurance and a safety and emissions inspection every 24 months for light-duty vehicles. Its lemon law covers new vehicles for one year or 15,000 miles, and the local motor vehicle excise tax has been phased out.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Rhode Island's term of protection in R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.2-1 is one year or 15,000 miles, and the presumption is in § 31-5.2-5. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, during that term is the test, and the manufacturer also gets one more cure of not more than seven calendar days. Report the nonconformity during the term of protection. The extra seven days starts when the manufacturer first knows the four-repair or 30-day limit has been met.
emissionsDetails: Gas and diesel light-duty vehicles take the emissions test with the safety inspection every 24 months. A new vehicle is exempt for two years from purchase or until 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: A light-duty vehicle of 8,500 pounds or less must pass a safety and emissions inspection at least once every 24 months. The fee for that inspection is $55.
evIncentiveDetails: DRIVE EV offers rebates on vehicles bought or leased from a licensed Rhode Island dealer: $3,000 for a new battery electric or fuel cell vehicle and $2,000 for a new plug-in hybrid, or $2,500 and $1,750 used, with price caps of $75,000 new and $55,000 used. DRIVE+ adds up to $1,500 for income-qualified residents, and PowerUpRI helps pay for home chargers.
registrationFeeRange: $30 a year up to 4,000 lb gross weight
registrationNotes: A two-year passenger renewal also adds a $3.50 technology surcharge for each year. It adds a $20 department of transportation surcharge for each year. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $100 per registration year. A non-plug-in hybrid pays an additional $50 per registration year.
lemonLawCitation: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.2-5; term of protection defined in § 31-5.2-1
lemonArbitration: The attorney general's Motor Vehicle Arbitration Board hears lemon-law disputes under R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.2-7.1. The consumer pays a $20 filing fee, the board decides within 90 days after the dispute is found eligible, and a manufacturer that appeals must post a bond for the award plus $2,500.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A battery-electric vehicle pays an additional $200 per registration year.

name: South Carolina
description: South Carolina requires 25/50/25 liability insurance plus uninsured motorist coverage, and registration runs two years at $40 for a passenger car. A one-time infrastructure maintenance fee of 5%, capped at $500, applies when a vehicle is first titled or registered, and the lemon law covers new vehicles for 12 months or 12,000 miles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: South Carolina, in S.C. Code §§ 56-28-30 and 56-28-40, asks for a report within the first 12 months or 12,000 miles, while the presumption counts repairs and days during the express warranty. The presumption is met by three repairs aimed at the same problem, or by 30 calendar days the car spends out of service. If the manufacturer clearly said at the sale that written notice is required, send that notice so it can make a final repair. It then has ten business days to name a franchised shop and ten business days after delivery to attempt the repair.
registrationFeeRange: $40 biennial for most vehicles
registrationNotes: The infrastructure maintenance fee is 5 percent of the purchase price and is capped at $500, and new residents pay a flat $250. County property tax must be paid before registration.
lemonLawCitation: S.C. Code Ann. § 56-28-40; repair term in § 56-28-30
lemonArbitration: If the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure that substantially complies with 16 C.F.R. part 703, S.C. Code § 56-28-60 requires the consumer to use it before the refund or replacement remedy applies. Section 56-28-90 lets the Department of Consumer Affairs establish a five-member state arbitration board by regulation for manufacturers without such a procedure. A lawsuit must be filed within three years of delivery.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A vehicle powered exclusively by electricity or hydrogen pays a $120 biennial road use fee on top of registration, and a hybrid pays $60 (S.C. Code § 56-3-645).

name: South Dakota
description: South Dakota requires 25/50/25 liability insurance plus uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage, and charges a 4% excise tax on vehicle purchases in place of sales tax. Annual license fees depend on shipping weight and drop once a vehicle is 10 years old, and the lemon law covers new vehicles for one year or 12,000 miles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: South Dakota's rights period in SDCL 32-6D-1 and 32-6D-5 is one year or 12,000 miles, and the problem has to start during that period. Repairs that count toward the presumption can run out to 24 months or 24,000 miles, so long as one attempt happened during the rights period. The test is four repairs plus a final attempt by the manufacturer, or 30 calendar days out of service with that final attempt included. Before a lawsuit, mail a certified demand to correct the problem; once the presumption is already met, the manufacturer has seven calendar days to designate a facility and 14 calendar days after the car arrives to finish the repair.
registrationFeeRange: Based on weight and age
registrationNotes: A noncommercial vehicle under 10 years old pays $36, $72, $108, or $144 for 12 months by shipping weight. The same weight classes pay $25.20, $50.40, $75.60, or $100.80 once the vehicle is 10 years or older. The motor vehicle excise tax is 4 percent of the purchase price, and counties may add a wheel tax.
lemonLawCitation: SDCL 32-6D-5; lemon law rights period defined in SDCL 32-6D-1
lemonArbitration: Before suing, the consumer must send the manufacturer a certified-mail notice of the nonconforming condition. If the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure conducted in South Dakota that complies with federal rules, SDCL 32-6D-6 requires the consumer to use it first. A lawsuit must be filed within three years of delivery.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric motor vehicle pays an additional $100 annual fee at registration under SDCL 32-5-188, as amended in 2026.

name: Tennessee
description: Tennessee requires 25/50/25 liability insurance, and auto policies include uninsured motorist coverage unless you reject it in writing. Emissions testing ended in 2022. The lemon law covers new vehicles for the warranty term or one year after delivery, whichever ends first.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage (Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-12-102(12)(D), for proof required after December 31, 2022)
lemonLawSummary: Tenn. Code Ann. §§ 55-24-101(7) and 55-24-105 call the coverage a term of protection. It lasts for the express warranty or for one year after delivery, whichever finishes first, and miles do not shorten it. Inside that term, three repairs of the same problem or 30 calendar days out of service is the presumption. Send certified mail before you go further, and if the presumption is already met the manufacturer gets one more chance of not more than ten days.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is no longer required in Tennessee. The county clerk registration guide says the requirement ended in February 2022. Davidson County ended its program on February 5, 2022. EPA removed the inspection-and-maintenance programs for Davidson, Sumner, Rutherford, Williamson, Wilson, and Hamilton counties from the state plan.
registrationFeeRange: $26.50 standard passenger plate, plus county fees
registrationNotes: Vehicle purchases pay the 7% state sales tax on the full price, a local option tax of up to 2.75% on the first $1,600 in 93 of 95 counties, and the 2.75% state single-article tax on the portion from $1,600.01 to $3,200. Counties may also charge a wheel tax.
titleFee: $5.50 state title fee plus $8.50 county clerk fee
lemonArbitration: Before claiming a refund or replacement, the consumer must notify the manufacturer by certified mail under Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-24-105. If the manufacturer has a qualifying informal dispute settlement procedure under 16 CFR Part 703 and notifies the consumer of it, § 55-24-106 requires the consumer to use it first; the Attorney General and Reporter determines on application whether a mechanism qualifies.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: At each renewal, all-electric vehicles pay an extra $200 through 2026 and $274 in 2027, and hybrids and plug-in hybrids pay $100 through 2027, with annual inflation adjustments from 2028 (Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-4-116).

name: Texas
description: Texas requires liability insurance. Personal-vehicle safety inspections ended on January 1, 2025. Registration includes a $7.50 inspection-program replacement fee, and emissions testing applies to gasoline vehicles in 17 counties.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Tex. Occ. Code § 2301.605 sets the presumption before the express warranty expires or before 24 months or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. The same nonconformity after four or more repairs is one path. A serious safety hazard after two or more repairs is the second path. A nonconformity that still substantially impairs use or market value after 30 or more cumulative days out of service is the third path. Subsection (b) extends those periods for war, invasion, strike, fire, flood, or another natural disaster, and subsection (c) leaves out any days the manufacturer or distributor lends a comparable vehicle while a franchised dealer repairs the owner's car. An order under § 2301.606(c) requires written notice of the defect and a chance for the manufacturer, converter, or distributor to cure.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing applies to gasoline vehicles registered in Brazoria, Collin, Dallas, Denton, El Paso, Ellis, Fort Bend, Galveston, Harris, Johnson, Kaufman, Montgomery, Parker, Rockwall, Tarrant, Travis, and Williamson counties. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this test. Bexar County gasoline vehicles that are 2 to 24 model years old start emissions testing on November 1, 2026.
safetyInspectionDetails: Personal-vehicle safety inspections ended on January 1, 2025, under HB 3297. Non-commercial vehicles pay a $7.50 inspection-program replacement fee at registration. A qualifying new passenger car or light truck pays $16.75 once, covering two years. Commercial vehicles still need a safety inspection and do not pay the replacement fee.
evIncentiveDetails: The 2026 Texas Light-Duty Motor Vehicle Purchase or Lease Incentive round for EVs is closed.
registrationFeeRange: $50.75 base fee for a vehicle with a gross weight of 6,000 pounds or less, plus state and county fees
registrationNotes: Register within 30 days of buying a vehicle or moving to Texas. A 6.25 percent motor vehicle sales tax applies to retail purchases, and a new resident pays a $90 use tax on a vehicle already registered in their name elsewhere.
lemonArbitration: A lemon-law complaint goes to the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles under Occupations Code Chapter 2301, Subchapter M, with a $35 filing fee. It is due within six months after the earliest of the warranty's end, 24 months after delivery, or 24,000 miles. Staff try mediation, and an unresolved complaint is heard by the department's Office of Administrative Hearings.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric-only vehicle of 10,000 pounds or less pays an extra $400 at the first registration of a new vehicle and $200 at each later registration or renewal under Tex. Transp. Code § 502.360.

name: Utah
description: Utah requires 30/65/25 liability insurance with personal injury protection, and emissions testing applies in Cache, Davis, Salt Lake, Utah, and Weber counties. Safety inspections apply to commercial vehicles and to certain first-time registrations, such as salvage vehicles and street-legal ATVs.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $65,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage, or $90,000 combined, for policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025 (Utah Code § 31A-22-304(2)), plus $3,000 PIP
lemonLawSummary: Utah Code § 13-20-5 starts from the express warranty and from the first anniversary of delivery, and it uses whichever of those dates arrives sooner. The section does not limit the presumption by miles. A reasonable number of attempts is four tries at the same problem, or 30 business days the car is out for repair. Section 13-20-3 is the report rule: tell the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer during the warranty or during that same year.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is a registration prerequisite in Cache, Davis, Salt Lake, Utah, and Weber counties. Frequency depends on the county and the model year. Electric vehicles are exempt.
safetyInspectionDetails: Under Utah Code § 41-1a-205, a safety inspection is required at the first registration of a street-legal ATV, street-legal novel vehicle, salvage vehicle, or roadable aircraft. Commercial vehicles, buses or vans for hire, taxicabs, and certain vehicles with three or more axles or pulling trailers must display a safety inspection certificate.
registrationFeeRange: $58.25 adjusted 2026 passenger-vehicle fee (the statute sets $44, indexed to inflation each January 1)
registrationNotes: Register within 60 days of establishing Utah residency. An age-based uniform fee in lieu of property tax also applies: $150 for model years 2024 through 2026, then $110, $80, $50, and $10 for older vehicles.
plateFee: Set in the DMV fee schedule
lemonArbitration: If the manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement program that complies with 16 C.F.R. Part 703, Utah Code § 13-20-7 requires using it before the refund and replacement remedies apply. Under § 13-20-6, a consumer may sue only after the Division of Consumer Protection has investigated and evaluated the claim.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Electric vehicles pay an extra registration fee equal to the road usage charge cap ($180 a year in 2026, $280 from January 1, 2027), or can enroll in UDOT's per-mile Road Usage Charge Program instead. Hybrids and plug-in hybrids pay smaller additional fees.

name: Vermont
description: Vermont requires 25/50/10 liability coverage with uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage of at least $50,000/$100,000, plus an annual safety and emissions inspection. The state has adopted California's vehicle emissions standards, and battery electric cars move to a mileage-based user fee on January 1, 2027.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Vermont's presumption in 9 V.S.A. § 4172(g) is tied to the express warranty, and at least the first repair attempt has to happen while that warranty is still in effect. Three repairs of the same problem, documented on written repair orders and generally at the same dealer, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the test. A car available to the owner for a major part of the day isn't counted as out of service. After a reasonable repair attempt or after those 30 days, § 4173 says to notify the manufacturer in writing and choose arbitration, and the manufacturer gets one final repair chance before the hearing.
emissionsDetails: The emissions check is part of the annual inspection for a covered gasoline vehicle. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Every motor vehicle registered in Vermont must be inspected once each year. The inspection manual includes an OBD-II test for a vehicle 16 model years old or newer with a gross vehicle weight rating of 8,500 pounds or less. The station sets the inspection charge.
registrationFeeRange: $91 for one year
registrationNotes: A two-year gas or diesel registration is $167. A replacement plate is $15, and a set of two is $29. Purchase and use tax is 6 percent of the taxable cost under 32 V.S.A. § 8903, and the Commissioner can set the taxable cost at the J.D. Power clean trade-in value when the price doesn't reflect actual value.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: The one-year registration for an electric automobile is $178. A two-year electric registration is $341. Those DMV amounts include the clean air fund fee and the EV infrastructure fee. From January 1, 2027, battery electric cars pay a mileage-based user fee of $0.014 per mile, capped at $178 per reporting period, under 23 V.S.A. ch. 43.
lemonArbitration: Under 9 V.S.A. § 4173, the consumer's written notice elects either the manufacturer's dispute settlement mechanism or the Vermont Motor Vehicle Arbitration Board, and the choice is binding. The hearing must be held within 45 days of the notice, with up to 30 more days for good cause. The consumer pays no fees under § 4175, and the Board decides within 30 days under § 4174.

name: Virginia
description: Virginia requires 50/100/25 liability coverage for policies effective on or after January 1, 2025, along with uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage. Every registered vehicle needs an annual safety inspection, and vehicles garaged in Northern Virginia also need a biennial emissions test.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage (policies effective on or after January 1, 2025)
lemonLawSummary: Virginia's lemon-law rights period in Va. Code §§ 59.1-207.11 and 59.1-207.13(B) is 18 months after delivery, with no mileage cap, and it can run longer if the manufacturer was notified and the problem is still unrepaired at the end. The presumption is three repairs of the same problem, one repair of a serious safety defect, or 30 calendar days out of service, unless the repairs could not be performed for reasons beyond the manufacturer's control. A serious safety defect means a life-threatening malfunction that interferes with ordinary control of the car or creates a risk of fire or explosion. Notify the manufacturer of the need for repair unless it was already notified, and if the presumption is already met the manufacturer gets up to 15 more days to correct it; the warranty or owner's manual has to disclose that written notification is required.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is a separate biennial test. It is required in Arlington, Fairfax, Loudoun, Prince William, and Stafford counties and in the cities of Alexandria, Fairfax, Falls Church, Manassas, and Manassas Park. A new vehicle is exempt for four years. The maximum fee is $30 under Va. Code § 46.2-1182. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: An annual safety inspection is required statewide. A station may charge no more than $20 for a non-commercial vehicle, and the charge is not mandatory. The safety inspection does not include the emissions test.
registrationFeeRange: $30.75 at 4,000 lb or less, or $35.75 from 4,001 to 6,500 lb
registrationNotes: Registration adds $2 when the vehicle is garaged in a locality that requires the emissions test, and localities in the DMV's Local Vehicle Registration Program may add local fees. The motor vehicle sales and use tax is 4.15% of the sale price, with a $75 minimum. New residents have 30 days to title and register.
lemonLawCitation: Va. Code § 59.1-207.13(B); lemon law rights period defined in § 59.1-207.11
lemonArbitration: Under Va. Code § 59.1-207.15, using a manufacturer's informal dispute settlement procedure is the consumer's choice. If that procedure awards a refund or replacement, the manufacturer has 40 days to comply. Under § 59.1-207.13(E), the owner notifies the manufacturer of the needed repair unless it already knows, and the manufacturer gets up to 15 more days once the presumption is in place. A consumer who wins a civil action under § 59.1-207.14 recovers attorney's fees, expert witness fees and court costs.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays a highway use fee of $135.63. The Virginia DMV chart sets that annual amount for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

name: Washington
description: Washington requires 25/50/10 liability coverage, and insurers must include underinsured motorist coverage and offer personal injury protection unless you reject them in writing. The state emission-check program ended on January 1, 2020, so registration no longer depends on an emissions test. Plug-in vehicles pay $225 in extra fees at each annual renewal.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Washington sets eligibility in RCW 19.118.021(6) at two years or 24,000 miles, and the written warranty used for the presumption in RCW 19.118.041(2) is at least one year or 12,000 miles. For a car that is not a motor home, the presumption is two repairs of the same serious safety defect, two or more different serious safety defects each repaired at least once within a 12-month period, four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service with at least 15 of those days during the written warranty. A motor home uses one serious-safety repair plus a final attempt, three repairs plus a final attempt, or 60 days out of service. Make a written request to the manufacturer before a replacement or repurchase; a motor-home owner sends written notice so the manufacturers can make one last coordinated attempt after one serious-safety repair, three attempts, or 30 days out.
emissionsDetails: Washington's emission-check program ended on January 1, 2020. Vehicle owners no longer need an emissions test to renew registration. The Department of Ecology repealed the obsolete testing rules in 2021. Driving a vehicle with modified emissions equipment, or a vehicle that smokes, is still illegal.
evIncentiveDetails: Washington's EV sales and use tax exemption for vehicle sales expired July 31, 2025. In October 2026, the Department of Commerce opened a request for proposals to administer a new $5 million point-of-sale EV rebate program, with a project period starting January 2027.
registrationFeeRange: $30 license tab
registrationNotes: Passenger vehicles also pay a $10 additional weight fee. A plate transfer is $10. Filing ($6) and service ($11) fees are charged in addition to the license tab, and DOL lists a basic renewal fee of $43.25. Inside the Sound Transit district, the RTA excise tax is 1.1 percent of depreciated value.
lemonLawCitation: RCW 19.118.041(2); eligibility period defined in RCW 19.118.021(6)
lemonArbitration: An owner requests arbitration from the Attorney General under RCW 19.118.090, within 30 months of the original retail delivery, and a manufacturer must arbitrate once the Attorney General accepts the dispute. The board holds a hearing within 45 days of assignment and decides within 60 days. Under RCW 19.118.080, the owner goes through the board, or a manufacturer's informal procedure under RCW 19.118.150, before suing.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: At annual renewal, DOL lists an electric-car fee of $100, an electric-car fee of $50, and a transportation electrification fee of $75. Together those renewal fees are $225.

name: West Virginia
description: West Virginia requires 25/50/25 liability coverage plus uninsured motorist coverage at the same minimums, and a safety inspection every two years. Electric vehicles pay a $200 annual fee on top of registration, and plug-in hybrids pay $100.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: The presumption in W. Va. Code § 46A-6A-5 stops at the end of the express warranty or at one year after delivery, whichever date is sooner. Miles do not limit it. A different clock, the repair duty in § 46A-6A-3, runs for the longer of those two periods. Three repairs of the same problem, 30 calendar days out of service, or one unsuccessful repair of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, meets the presumption, but only after written notice and at least one chance to cure.
safetyInspectionDetails: West Virginia requires a safety inspection every 24 months under W. Va. Code § 17C-16-4, effective January 1, 2024. The maximum sticker fee is $19 for that two-year period. The inspection covers brakes, steering, tires, lights, glass, exhaust, horn, and mirrors.
registrationFeeRange: $51.50 for Class A vehicles
registrationNotes: A 6 percent titling tax applies to a purchase (§ 11-15-3c), or a flat $30 when the net price is under $500. New residents have 30 days to title and register, and the titling tax is waived for a vehicle already titled in their name in their previous state.
lemonArbitration: Under W. Va. Code § 46A-6A-8, the Attorney General sets rules for third-party dispute mechanisms supervised by its Consumer Protection Division. If a qualified process exists and the owner gets timely written notice of it, the owner uses it before filing suit under § 46A-6A-4. Written notice to the manufacturer and at least one chance to cure under § 46A-6A-5 are also needed for the presumption to apply.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: Under W. Va. Code § 17A-10-3c, a vehicle that runs exclusively on electricity pays a $200 annual fee, and one that runs on electricity and petrochemical fuels pays $100. Hydrogen and natural gas vehicles pay $200. The fees are in addition to regular registration fees.

name: Wisconsin
description: Wisconsin requires 25/50/10 liability coverage plus uninsured motorist coverage of $25,000/$50,000 and $1,000 in medical payments coverage. Vehicles kept in seven southeastern counties need emissions tests, and electric vehicles pay a $175 surcharge on top of the $85 automobile registration fee.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Wis. Stat. § 218.0171(1)(h) starts the clock at the end of the express warranty or one year after the first delivery, whichever happens sooner, and miles are not part of the test. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 days out of service because of warranty problems, is a reasonable attempt to repair, and time lost to a flood, other natural disaster, war, invasion, fire, or strike does not count. A car the owner is still driving counts as out of service only when a problem substantially affects use or safety and has already had at least two repair attempts. After a reasonable attempt fails, give the manufacturer the form described in the statute before it has to refund or replace the car.
emissionsDetails: WisDOT requires emissions tests for vehicles customarily kept in Kenosha, Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Racine, Sheboygan, Washington and Waukesha counties: model years 1996 to 2006 under 8,501 lbs GVWR (gasoline, natural gas or hybrid) and 2007 and newer up to 14,000 lbs GVWR (including diesel). Tests can be due every other year before renewal and within 45 days of a purchase, title owner change or new-resident transfer.
registrationFeeRange: $85 for an automobile
registrationNotes: Towns, villages, cities and counties may add an annual flat registration fee under Wis. Stat. § 341.35. A hybrid electric automobile or truck registered at 8,000 pounds or less pays a $75 surcharge. Title is $207 plus a $7.50 supplemental fee.
lemonArbitration: Under Wis. Stat. § 218.0171(3), if a manufacturer has an informal dispute settlement procedure certified by the Wisconsin Department of Transportation, the consumer must use it before suing. To be certified, the procedure must comply with 16 CFR Part 703 and require the statutory refund or replacement remedy, and WisDOT publishes an annual evaluation of certified programs.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric automobile or light truck at or below 8,000 pounds pays a $175 surcharge.

name: Wyoming
description: Wyoming requires 25/50/20 liability coverage, and policies must include uninsured motorist coverage unless the named insured rejects it. Registration combines a county fee based on factory price and age with a $30 state fee for passenger cars, and plug-in vehicles pay an annual decal fee.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Wyoming's lemon law, Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 40-17-101, places the repair duty and the presumption within one year after delivery. More than three repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption. During that year, tell the manufacturer, its agent, or the dealer authorized to do the repair. The refund or replacement remedy is withheld if the owner has not finished a manufacturer's informal dispute program that meets federal rules.
registrationFeeRange: $30 state fee plus a county fee
registrationNotes: The county fee is 3 percent of a declining share of factory price, with a $5 minimum. A replacement plate after loss is $8.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An all-electric vehicle pays a $100 annual decal fee and a plug-in hybrid pays $50 under Wyo. Stat. § 31-3-102(a)(xxiii)-(xxiv).
lemonArbitration: Under Wyo. Stat. Ann. § 40-17-101(f), the refund or replacement remedy isn't available to a consumer who hasn't exhausted the manufacturer's informal dispute settlement procedure, if one exists and complies with federal law (16 CFR Part 703). Part 703 programs can't charge consumers a fee, and their decisions aren't binding.

name: Washington DC
description: Washington DC has some of the most comprehensive vehicle ownership regulations in the nation. As the nation's capital, DC requires liability insurance, annual vehicle inspections, and offers generous incentives for electric vehicle adoption as part of its sustainability goals.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: D.C. Code § 50-502(d) uses the first 18,000 miles or two years after delivery to the original purchaser. Four repairs of a non-safety problem, one repair of a safety-related problem, or 30 days out of service, is the presumption, and those 30 days can be extended for a war, invasion, strike, fire, flood, or similar disaster. While that window is open, tell the manufacturer, an agent, or an authorized dealer, and if the agent or dealer is the one who receives it, that person has seven days to forward certified mail to the manufacturer. A lawsuit waits until the claim has been submitted to the Board of Consumer Claims Arbitration under § 50-503.
emissionsDetails: Private passenger vehicles need an emissions inspection every two years. The inspection fee is $35. A fully electric passenger vehicle can receive a non-expiring inspection sticker. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Private passenger vehicles in the District of Columbia do not take a safety inspection.
registrationFeeRange: $70, $175, $300, or $550 by weight class
registrationNotes: Those passenger amounts took effect on March 30, 2026. Regular tag replacement is $15. A hybrid does not qualify for the battery-electric registration rate.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
